findings.title: Aggressive and Uncapped Liquidated Damages
findings.deviation: LDs are 2% of Total Contract Value per day, whereas AtliQ requires 0.5% of the affected milestone per week capped at 5%.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces excessive financial penalties that could quickly exceed the total project margin for even minor delays.
findings.quote: Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages Not Sole Remedy
findings.deviation: The clause states LDs are in addition to actual damages, rather than the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
findings.impact: The client could collect both the fixed penalty and additional damages for the same delay, leading to double recovery.
findings.quote: Liquidated damages under this Article are in addition to and not in lieu of Client's right to recover its actual damages
findings.counterPosition: Liquidated damages shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Unlimited Liability for AtliQ
findings.deviation: The agreement imposes unlimited liability on AtliQ while capping the client's liability at fees paid.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces open-ended financial risk for any claim, which exceeds the standard 1x fees cap.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; data-protection liability under a separate super-cap.

findings.title: Indemnification for Client's Own Negligence
findings.deviation: AtliQ is required to indemnify the client even for losses caused by the client's own negligence.
findings.impact: AtliQ could be held financially responsible for errors or omissions actually committed by the client.
findings.quote: in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence.

findings.title: No Payment for Work in Progress
findings.deviation: The client refuses to pay for any unaccepted deliverables or work in progress upon termination for convenience.
findings.impact: AtliQ could perform significant work and incur costs without any right to payment if the client terminates early.
findings.quote: Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs.

findings.title: IP Vesting on Creation
findings.deviation: Intellectual property rights vest in the client upon creation rather than upon receipt of payment.
findings.impact: The client would own the output even if they fail to pay AtliQ for the services provided.
findings.quote: shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.
findings.counterPosition: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment.

findings.title: Assignment of Pre-Existing Materials
findings.deviation: The contract assigns ownership of AtliQ's pre-existing materials to the client if they are incorporated into deliverables.
findings.impact: AtliQ risks losing its proprietary tools and background IP to the client.
findings.quote: Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein... any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable
findings.counterPosition: AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.

findings.title: Cyber Insurance Limit Exceeds Cover
findings.deviation: The contract requires $5,000,000 in cyber insurance, but AtliQ only maintains $1,000,000.
findings.impact: AtliQ is in immediate breach of the agreement upon signature unless it increases its insurance coverage.
findings.counterPosition: Align required limits with current cover ($1,000,000).

findings.title: Short Notice for Convenience
findings.deviation: The notice period for convenience termination is only 7 days, below the 30-day standard.
findings.impact: AtliQ has very little time to reallocate staff and resources if the client exits the project.
findings.quote: upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor.
findings.counterPosition: Provide for a mutual notice period of at least 30 days.

findings.title: Broad Set-off Rights
findings.deviation: The client may set off amounts across unrelated agreements.
findings.impact: Payments for this project could be withheld due to disputes on completely separate contracts.
findings.quote: Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.
findings.counterPosition: Set-off limited to undisputed amounts under this agreement.

findings.title: Invoicing Waiver Period
findings.deviation: Invoices not submitted within 90 days are deemed waived.
findings.impact: AtliQ loses the right to be paid for validly performed work if administrative delays occur in invoicing.
findings.quote: Invoices not submitted within ninety (90) days after acceptance shall be deemed waived.

fine.note: NDA obligations in Article 6 are mutual and include standard exclusions.
Offshore data restrictions in Clause 12.4 allow for de-identified access in client environments, matching the playbook standard.
The 12-month performance warranty on deliverables is consistent with industry standards.
